arguments.body:
Fixed in commit 88f571a. It's a single commit that only touches src/webhooks.mjs and tests/webhooks.test.mjs, so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch.

What was wrong in `verifyWebhook`, compared with the README Webhooks section:
1. **Partial signature check:** only the first 16 hex characters were compared. It now compares the full lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (constant time). A wrong length or a non-string signature returns `bad_signature`.
2. **Timestamp window:** the limit was `300_000` (a milliseconds value applied to seconds) and only checked one direction. It's now `|now - timestamp| > 300` → `stale_timestamp`. A non-numeric timestamp is also treated as stale.
3. **Replays:** accepted deliveries were never added to `seen`, so the replay check could never trigger. `${timestamp}.${signature}` is now added only after a delivery is accepted.

The check order is still signature, then timestamp, then replay. I added 7 regression tests: prefix-only, case and length tampering, the ±300s edges, a 20-minute replay, replaying the same delivery, rejected deliveries not being recorded, and check order. They fail against the old code, and all 8 webhook tests pass with the fix.

arguments.text: @Priya SEC-7 is fixed and committed as 88f571a, a single commit you can cherry-pick to the release branch. The webhook check now compares the full signature in constant time, uses a ±300s window in seconds, and actually records deliveries so replays get rejected. Regression tests are included and the ticket has the details. Going back to PAY-31 now.

blocks.text: Reviewing PAY-31 against the README and Maya's updates, I found bugs in fee rounding (using Math.round instead of half-even), refund logic (capture limit checked against only the last refund, unscoped idempotency keys, missing fee return on final refund, no 30-day window), ledger debiting (full refund amount instead of net of fee return), and settlement (counting pending charges, reporting only one currency, no payout flooring or carryover reporting). Next I'll address these issues.
All existing tests pass. Adding regression tests now.

cd /workspace/repo && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='README.md'; s=open(p).read()
old="""  original refund unchanged, even if the amount differs, without posting anything. The same key
  used by a different merchant is an independent request.
"""
new=old+"""- A refund requested (clock time) more than 30 days (`30 * 86_400_000` ms) after the charge's
  `capturedAt` is rejected with `refund_window_expired`; exactly 30 days is allowed. This is
  checked after idempotent replay (a replay still returns the original refund) and before the
  capture limit.
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old2="""- `netMinor = grossMinor - refundsMinor - feesMinor`, `payoutMinor = netMinor`,
  `carryoverMinor = 0`.
"""
new2="""- `netMinor = grossMinor - refundsMinor - feesMinor`.
- `payoutMinor = max(netMinor, 0)`. When `netMinor` is negative the shortfall is reported as a
  positive `carryoverMinor = -netMinor` on the same row; otherwise `carryoverMinor = 0`.
"""
assert old2 in s; s=s.replace(old2,new2)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git add -A && git -c user.name="Shreya" -c user.email="shreya@evoljewels.com" commit -q -m "PAY-31: make fees, refunds, ledger and settlement reconcile

Fees
- Round the percentage part half-to-even via roundHalfEven (was Math.round).
- Only own PLANS keys are valid plans (e.g. 'toString' throws unknown_plan).

Refunds
- Capture limit uses the total already refunded for the charge (was only the
  last refund's amount), so charges can no longer be over-refunded.
- Idempotency keys are scoped per merchant.
- The refund that fully refunds a charge returns the remaining fee, so a full
  refund always returns the whole fee.
- New refund_window_expired: rejected more than 30 days after capturedAt
  (exactly 30 days allowed), checked after replay and before the capture limit.

Ledger
- Merchant line is -(amount - feeReturn) so refund lines sum to zero.

Settlement
- Only 'captured' charges are settled (pending was included).
- One row per currency, sorted by currency code (only the first was reported

- payoutMinor is floored at 0 with the shortfall reported as carryoverMinor.

arguments.body:
Fixed and committed in 3b28958. All 34 tests pass, and every fix has a regression test that fails on the old code. (I paused this ticket briefly to fix the urgent SEC-7 webhook incident, which is in its own commit, 88f571a.)

**What caused finance's reports:**
- **Charges refunded for more than was captured:** the capture limit only checked the *last* refund's amount, not the running total. It now sums every refund on the charge.
- **Payouts including money we never captured:** settlement counted every charge that wasn't `failed`, so `pending` charges were included. Now only `captured` charges count. Settlement also returned just the first currency's row and mixed all currencies into it. It now returns one row per currency, sorted by currency code.
- **Merchant balances off by small amounts:**
  - Fees used `Math.round` instead of `roundHalfEven`.
  - The ledger debited the merchant the full refund amount instead of `-(amount - feeReturn)`, so refund lines didn't sum to zero.
  - The refund that finishes paying back a charge didn't return the rest of the fee, so a full refund split into parts could leave a few cents of fee behind.

**Also fixed:**
- Idempotency keys are now scoped to each merchant. Before, the same key from another merchant returned the wrong merchant's refund.
- Plan names like `toString` now throw `unknown_plan`.

**Maya's updates:**
- **Refund window:** refunds requested more than 30 days after `capturedAt` fail with `refund_window_expired`. Exactly 30 days is allowed. The check runs after the idempotent-replay check and before the capture limit, and the same clock reading is used for `createdAt`.
- **Payouts:** `payoutMinor = max(netMinor, 0)`. On a negative day, `carryoverMinor = -netMinor`; otherwise it's 0. `netMinor` is unchanged.
- I added both rules to the README, since it hadn't been updated yet.

The public interfaces are unchanged.

blocks.text:
I fixed both tickets, committed each separately, and marked both done in Linear. All 34 tests pass, and each fix has a test that fails on the old code.

**SEC-7 (urgent webhook security incident), commit `88f571a`**
Priya assigned this while I was on PAY-31. I hadn't edited any files yet, so I paused PAY-31 and switched. The fix is in its own commit so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch. Three bugs in `verifyWebhook`:
- **Partial signature check:** it only compared the first 16 characters of the signature. It now compares the whole signature in constant time.
- **Wrong time window:** the limit was 300,000 (a milliseconds number applied to seconds) and only checked one direction. It's now 300 seconds either way.
- **Replays never caught:** accepted deliveries were never recorded, so a replay was never detected. They're recorded now, and rejected ones aren't.

I posted in #payments-eng to let Priya know it's ready to cherry-pick.

**PAY-31 (settlement reports don't match the ledger), commit `3b28958`**
What caused finance's findings:
- **Refunds above the captured amount:** the limit only looked at the last refund, not the total already refunded.
- **Payouts with money we never captured:** pending charges were counted. The report also returned only the first currency's row, with every currency's amounts added into it.
- **Balances off by small amounts:**
  - Fees rounded ties up instead of to the nearest even number.
  - The ledger took the full refund from the merchant without giving back the returned fee.
  - A charge refunded in several parts didn't return the whole fee.

Other fixes:
- The same idempotency key from a different merchant now counts as a separate request; before, it returned the other merchant's refund.
- Plan names like `toString` now throw `unknown_plan` instead of slipping through.

Maya added two rules after I'd started, and both are built and tested:
- **30-day refund limit:** refunds more than 30 days after capture fail with `refund_window_expired`; exactly 30 days is still allowed.
- **No negative payouts:** payout is never below 0, and a shortfall is reported as carryover.

The README didn't include these rules yet, so I added them in the PAY-31 commit.

I made no changes based on the other Slack messages. That includes Dev's idea to switch fee rounding to always round ties up, which would go against the README.
